_comment: Every host here must ALSO be in the cloud environment's Allowed domains list, or fetches fail with HTTP 403 and x-deny-reason: host_not_allowed. The allowlisted flag records whether that has been done.
_verified: 2026-07-25 — every feed below was fetched live and parsed; item counts recorded in _note.

tier1_primary.name: OpenAI News
tier1_primary._note: 1050 items / 637 KB — full archive every fetch. Fine, but the largest download in the set.

tier1_primary.name: arXiv cs.AI
tier1_primary._note: Legitimately EMPTY on weekends — the feed declares <skipDays>Saturday,Sunday</skipDays>. Zero items on a Sat/Sun is correct behaviour, not a failure.

tier2_press.name: The Verge
tier2_press._note: HTTP 403 from the cloud sandbox, HTTP 200 from a residential IP with the same user-agent. Was an allowlist block until 2026-07-25; now the domain resolves and the origin refuses. That is outlet-side blocking of datacenter addresses, not something the network policy can fix. Do not re-diagnose it as an allowlist problem.

tier2_press.name: Ars Technica
tier2_press._note: HTTP 403 from the cloud sandbox, HTTP 200 from a residential IP. Same cause as The Verge: datacenter-IP blocking at the origin.

_removed.name: Anthropic News
_removed.reason: No public RSS feed as of 2026-07-25. Checked and 404: /rss.xml, /news/rss.xml, /feed.xml, /news/feed.xml, /news/rss, /index.xml, /engineering/rss.xml; the news page declares no <link rel=alternate>. Anthropic stories still reach the pipeline via the press tier and via WebSearch. Do not re-add without verifying a live feed.

scoring._comment: Used to pick which story becomes a post. Sendability is weighted highest because DM shares are Instagram's strongest ranking signal in 2026.
